extracted.intended_audience: journalists, media professionals, and anyone seeking AEI press materials or to arrange interviews with AEI scholars
extracted.subtask_description: Institutional press-room guidance and exemplars for AEI press releases, media contacts, and in‑house broadcast/studio capabilities; useful for producing or contacting about AEI press materials. Covers contact procedures, release formatting conventions, and types of announcements AEI issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dateline and 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE' header
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases typically begin with a release header and dateline such as 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: Washington, DC (April 28, 2026)—'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example pattern used repeatedly on the page: 'FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE: Washington, DC (date)—The American Enterprise Institute (AEI) ... announced today that...'. Use an uppercase release marker and include the city (Washington, DC) and date in parentheses immediately following.

rubrics_metrics.name: Byline and date metadata ('BY' and 'ON')
rubrics_metrics.description: Each press item on the AEI press room shows metadata lines labeled 'BY' and 'ON' (author and publish date).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an author attribution line (BY) and a publication date line (ON) as part of the press-item metadata; examples: 'BY Robert Doar' and 'ON 28 Apr 26'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Headline format often prefaced with 'Press Release' or 'Release'
rubrics_metrics.description: Many headlines are presented with a prefix like 'Press Release:' or 'Release:' followed by the descriptive headline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a clear descriptive headline and optionally prefix with 'Press Release:' or 'Release:' to signal the item type (as in the page examples).

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead paragraph summarizing the announcement
rubrics_metrics.description: The lead paragraph succinctly states the news (who, what, where, when, and why) immediately after the dateline, e.g., 'The American Enterprise Institute (AEI) and Neighbors for a Better San Francisco announced today that...'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Start with a concise summary sentence that gives the core news and institutional affiliation. The AEI examples put this right after the dateline/header.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide relevant background and details (roles, titles, context)
rubrics_metrics.description: Releases supply supporting detail about people, roles, program descriptions, or study findings (e.g., announcing someone 'has joined AEI as a fellow' with previous positions and responsibilities).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include the new appointee's title, prior roles, relevant expertise, and context for the announcement; for reports, provide key findings or scope. AEI entries routinely include biographical sentences and program context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized press inquiries contact information
rubrics_metrics.description: AEI lists central press contact information: 'Press Department', 'Press Email: [email protected]', 'Press Phone: 202.862.5829'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make a clear, central contact point for press inquiries. The AEI page shows a press email and phone number for general press inquiries and encourages use of that contact for media requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designate media-relations contacts by policy area
rubrics_metrics.description: The page lists named media-relations staff (with email and phone) and specifies areas of responsibility — e.g., Brady Africk (general AEI/President), Lexi Baker (domestic policy, poverty, agriculture, housing, tech, energy), Hannah Bowen (economics and health care), Lyman Ortkiese (national security/foreign and defense policy), etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Direct media to the appropriate staff member for subject-matter interviews or materials. The page gives explicit points of contact and notes which policy areas each staffer covers; follow this routing for faster scheduling and relevant expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: How to request interviews and materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Instructions repeated on the page: 'If you are interested in booking an interview with an AEI scholar, please email AEI media services at [email protected] or call 202.862.5829.' and 'To schedule an interview with a scholar in any of the above policy areas or obtain comments, studies, and research materials, please email [email protected] or call [phone].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide explicit contact instructions in the release (email and phone) for interview bookings and for obtaining comments, studies, and research materials; mirror AEI's phrasing to set expectations for how to request interviews/materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describe in‑house broadcast/studio capabilities
rubrics_metrics.description: AEI documents its studios: 'full-service in-house broadcast facilities including a radio and TV studio' with features like 'VideoLink ReadyCam technology', professional lighting, two electronic backdrops, state-of-the-art audio equipment, and 'Comrex broadcasting technology'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If offering in‑house broadcast facilities, describe capabilities and technologies so producers know what to expect (live and taped interviews, remote transmission, backdrops, audio feed options). AEI specifies equipment and what each studio can accommodate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indicate availability of AEI event audio and podcast hosting
rubrics_metrics.description: The page notes the radio studio 'has the capability to transmit AEI event audio for radio via the Comrex system' and can be used for 'radio interviews, podcasts, and guest hosting of radio shows.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether event audio can be transmitted/delivered for radio/podcast distribution and how producers can access or arrange that service.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of 'Key takeaways' for data/analysis releases
rubrics_metrics.description: Research/data-focused releases may include a 'Key [month] Takeaways' section summarizing main findings (example: 'Key July Takeaways: The year-over-year home price appreciation (HPA) rates...').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For empirical reports or indices, include a short bulleted or labeled 'Key Takeaways' section that highlights main results for journalists and readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of announcements AEI issues (personnel, awards, reports, initiatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: AEI press-room content types shown include: announcements of scholars joining AEI, appointments and chairs, awards (Irving Kristol Award), program launches (centers, initiatives), conference notices, research reports, and indexes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Select the appropriate format/tone for the announcement type (personnel hires emphasize biography; awards include ceremony details; reports include findings and takeaways). AEI examples demonstrate distinct content emphases by announcement type.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard institutional dateline preference (Washington, DC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Most AEI releases use the dateline 'Washington, DC' in the header.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When AEI is the issuer, the dateline used in examples is Washington, DC; follow institutional convention unless the story location requires a different dateline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide media-team biographies and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The page supplies short bios for media-team members (education, role, responsibilities, areas promoted) alongside contact details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include brief bios for press-office staff so journalists know points of contact and their subject expertise; AEI shows educational background, role description, and which scholars/areas the staffer supports.
